title: Defined benefit / cash balance plans for high-income owners
summary: For owners with $300K+ consistent net income and a desire to shelter substantially more than 401(k) limits allow.
detailsHtml:
The opportunity

A defined benefit plan (DB) or cash balance plan allows contributions of $100,000–$300,000+ per year, depending on age and income. Older owners can contribute more (the plan must "fund" their retirement benefit, and older participants have less time to compound). This is the highest-limit retirement vehicle available to U.S. business owners.

The costs

Actuarial setup: $2,000–$5,000. Annual administration and actuarial: $3,000–$8,000. Required commitment of consistent funding (multi-year commitment to contributions; can be amended but not skipped easily). For very high earners, the tax savings can be hundreds of thousands annually — far exceeding the costs.

The employee cost

If you have employees, you'll typically need to provide some benefit to them too (varies by plan design — top-heavy testing applies). Combination cash balance + Safe Harbor 401(k) + profit sharing is often optimized to maximize owner contributions while meeting nondiscrimination tests.
